capitals.name: Bonga
capitals.note: "The Kingdom of Kaffa existed from 1390 to 1897 ... with its first capital at Bonga"; the page says Bonga was later replaced by Anderaccha though it kept its importance (no dates). Coordinates approximate (Bonga is not in the gazetteer).

correction.text: the Kingdom of Kaffa, bounded north by the Gojeb River and east by the Omo

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks Kaffa). "It was bounded to the north by the Gojeb River, beyond which lay the Gibe kingdoms", with the Omo to the east. The page gives no area. The region name Kaffa is not yet in the gazetteer (the ethiopian-empire dossier already uses it).

union.text: the Kingdom of Kaffa, bounded north by the Gojeb River and east by the Omo

correction.text: Kaffa with the annexed Gimira states of She, Benesho and Majango

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "Beginning with Gali Ginocho (1675-1710), the kings of Kaffa began to expand the borders of their kingdom", annexing the Gimira states of She, Benesho and Majango; Shagi Sherocho (1775-1795) "extended the boundaries of his kingdom as far as the Omo to the southeast"; "During the reign of King Hoti Gaocho (1798-1821), the territory of the Kaffa kings reached its maximum." The Oromo invasion of the 18th century cost "all territories north of the Gojeb". The page gives no area; the drawn shape is the Kaffa and Gimirra regions.

ledger.note: c. 1390: Minjo founds the Kingdom of Kaffa at Bonga. "The Kingdom of Kaffa was founded c.1390 by Minjo, who according to oral tradition ousted the Mato dynasty of 32 kings."

region.text: the Kingdom of Kaffa, bounded north by the Gojeb River and east by the Omo

ledger.note: Reign of Gali Ginocho, 1675-1710: Kaffa begins to expand. "Beginning with Gali Ginocho (1675-1710), the kings of Kaffa began to expand the borders of their kingdom"; the page names the annexed Gimira states but gives no year for each. 1675 is the start of the reign.

region.text: the Gimira states of She, Benesho and Majango

ledger.note: 18th century: Mecha Oromo invade and take the land north of the Gojeb. "Around the 18th century, the kingdom was invaded by the Mecha Oromos. Kaffa repelled the invasion, but all territories north of the Gojeb were lost." 1700 is a placeholder for the century.

region.text: the territories north of the Gojeb River, the Gibe kingdoms

ledger.note: Reign of Shagi Sherocho, 1775-1795: Kaffa reaches the Omo. "[Shagi Sherocho] extended the boundaries of his kingdom as far as the Omo to the southeast." Reign start used as the year.

region.text: the lands to the Omo in the south-east

ledger.note: September 1897: Kaffa falls to Menelik. "The kingdom was overrun and conquered in 1897"; Gaki Sherocho "was captured on 11 September 1897"; the attackers included Welde Giyorgis Aboye, Ras Damisse and Abba Jifar II of Jimma. The ethiopian-empire dossier has the gain in 1900.

region.text: the Kingdom of Kaffa, bounded north by the Gojeb River and east by the Omo

ledger.note: 1897: the Kingdom of Kaffa ends; "Kaffa was then held as a fief by Wolde Giyogis until 1914."

wars.name: Menelik's conquest of Kaffa

zones.text: the Kingdom of Kaffa, bounded north by the Gojeb River and east by the Omo

wars.outcome: Kaffa overrun in 1897 and annexed; Gaki Sherocho captured on 11 September 1897 and sent to Ankober.
wars.note: "Menelik had amassed many more guns." Welde Giyorgis Aboye, Ras Damisse and Abba Jifar II of Jimma were among the attackers.

wars.name: Kaffa-Amhara wars (1890 and 1893)
wars.outcome: The last king "had defeated two Amhara invasions of his kingdom in 1890 and 1893".

wars.name: Mecha Oromo invasion of Kaffa

zones.text: the territories north of the Gojeb

wars.outcome: Kaffa repelled the invasion but lost all territory north of the Gojeb River.

certainty.note: The Gojeb River (north) and the Omo (east) are the only boundaries named.

sources.title: Kingdom of Kaffa
sources.note: Founded c. 1390 by Minjo, expansion from 1675, maximum 1798-1821, Oromo invasion in the 18th century, Amhara invasions 1890 and 1893, conquest 1897, Gaki Sherocho captured 11 September 1897. No area.

notes:
New dossier: Cliopatria lacks Kaffa. One page opened (Kingdom of Kaffa; budget 1-2). Dates on the page: c. 1390 founding, reigns from 1675, 1775-1795, 1798-1821 (maximum), the 18th-century Oromo invasion, 1890 and 1893 Amhara invasions, 1897 conquest. Disagreement: the ethiopian-empire dossier (af-01-b) records the Kaffa gain in 1900 and a vassal_start in 1881; the page here says conquered 1897, held as a fief by Wolde Giyorgis until 1914. Counterpart strings: 'Mato dynasty', 'Gimira states (She, Benesho, Majango)', 'Oromo'; kingdom-of-jimma is named as a belligerent (Abba Jifar II of Jimma attacked with Menelik) and may get a dossier from a gap-filler. Gazetteer names needed: Kaffa (Kefa, the highlands between the Gojeb and the Omo, capital Bonga about 7.27 N 36.25 E), Gimirra (the Gimira lands, south-west Ethiopia).
Predecessor: the legendary Mato dynasty of 32 kings (oral tradition) has no dossier and is not listed in identity.predecessors.
